summary: Three measurements of the same LEAKY-minus-CLEAN_MATCHED contrast at achieved operating points spanning only 0.0030 AUROC differ in gap by 38.3x. The 48.6x operating-point decline measured in code/47's Sweep C is therefore a property of that synthetic harness and its single fixed mechanism, not a severity law that transports across harnesses or mechanisms. The operating point remains a strong severity MODIFIER within a harness and must be matched before two severity numbers are compared; it is not a predictor of severity across them.

probit_loglinear_interpolation.form: log gap = m * Phi^-1(achieved AUROC) + b
probit_loglinear_interpolation.note: Fit on ACHIEVED operating points, not nominal targets, because that is the coordinate on which the real harnesses are matched.

observations.name: real-feature checkpoint-only harness (code/43), capacity 128
observations.harness: real Mistral-7B/HaluEval features, checkpoint argmax only

observations.name: fidelity extension (code/49), capacity 128
observations.harness: real features, argmax + LR scheduler + early stopping on the same fold

what_this_does_not_show: This does not falsify the operating-point relationship. Within code/47's synthetic harness it is monotone and strongly fit, and it is reported as such. What fails is TRANSPORT: the relationship's slope and level are harness-specific. Two of the three measurements here also differ in leakage MECHANIC (argmax only versus argmax plus scheduler plus early stopping), so mechanism and harness are not separated by this comparison -- which is itself the point, since the paper had claimed the operating point moves severity more than mechanism differences do.
